title: The Parchment
subtitle: A magical medium, upon which every sentence written speaks a profound truth.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: We can't say for sure if this ritual was created by the last guest.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Fact is, you can find all kinds of unusual markings in this motel—most of them less than a month old. Very recent indeed.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: The maid said that there ain't many tourists these days, so my guess is that a group of skilled arcanists have left their work in every room.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Based on the markings I've seen so far, there were about three to five people in this group.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And was there a sheep-headed arcanist among them?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Well, that I don't know.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: What I can say, though, is that there was a sheep living in here. I saw some hoofprints on the hallway floor.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: It looked like someone had stayed in this motel with a sheep—sounds pretty odd, but I suppose it ain't too strange given the local farmland.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: But I'm sure this will catch your attention.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: We all know that sheep walk on four hooves.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: But the hoofprints I saw were different. They were small and delicate and, most importantly, followed the movement pattern of a human. Judging by the trail ...

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: The owner of the hoofprints was about the size of a slender kid, maybe 5 feet tall.
This description exactly matches the Foundation's report.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's it. That's the one I'm looking for.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Don't I know it—they can question my morals, but nobody can question my competence.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: So, may I enter your room now, Ms. Vertin?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Now, let's start with this little thing.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: The carvings are new. No sign of woodworm damage or moisture absorption.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: These splinters along the edge are extremely sharp. Mm?
She dips her finger into a dark red, crumbly residue.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Is this dried blood?
She rubs the granules between her finger and her thumb, reducing them to a fine powder.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Blood was used as the medium for this array.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The circle isn't fully closed here, and the lines are a bit uneven. Whoever drew this doesn't seem to be an expert.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You know how to deal with this, right?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: All you have to do is ask, boss. You might be surprised.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We need to destroy it as quickly as possible. I think it's been left by a dangerous occult group.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Hold on.
She places a pillow over the wood and pulls the trigger.
After a faint gunshot, the lingering light goes out.
*squelch*
Fresh blood oozes from the array, settling in the faded carvings.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is that blood?
The mercenary, unfazed, dips her finger into the red liquid and sniffs it.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Yup. The blood of an arcanist. So it can't be Kayla's.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Can you discern the owner's identity?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Hah, I ain't all-knowing. I can't identify people by their blood.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: No, I'll need more than just blood to find out who was here.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Mm?
She fishes out a dusty sheepskin journal from the gap between the cabinet and the wall.
She flips through the pages.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: "We are the beginning and the original source of metals."

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: "Through us, the highest tincture of art is brewed."

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: "There is neither a spring nor water like mine. I heal and help both the rich and the poor."

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: "Yet I am full of hurtful poison."

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: What the hell does that mean?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's a quote from a text on alchemy.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: "All challenges will be resolved with the provision of sufficient and high quality materials and the precise execution of the array."

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: "But where do we find these materials?"
She continues to flick through the journal, releasing the accumulated alchemical residue on its pages into the air.
On the last page, tortured words are scrawled on the paper. It looks like something a criminal would write in their final moments before their death sentence.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: "What was once sundered shall reunite."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *cough*
Her nose burns as barely visible sparks heat the air.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I've seen this handwriting before.

items.speaker: "Order" Follower I
items.text: And here. My phone number.
He hands over a dollar bill with a string of numbers scrawled along the blank space.
The mercenary pulls out the crumpled bill from her pocket, comparing the handwriting with that in the journal.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Yup. This is definitely the same.
*bang*

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: That sound. It's a Flying Arrow M1903 pistol.
Ahhh.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Kimberly? What's wrong with her now?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I better go check it out, boss. Something don't seem right. You coming?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: That Kimberly must've run into something.
